opus_produkce: Isa is stillness, the water held hard. Set beside Uruz, the two do not cancel — one is a body pushing, the other is ground that does not yield easily. But the reading you drew is Uruz alone, and Uruz holds the bog, not the ice. The bog gives way. It takes the strength differently than frozen ground would, and the effort shows in the lifting of a single hoof. What the next step meets is not yet in the image.

Isa is ice, the hold that stills a thing where it stands. Set beside Uruz, the two do not cancel. One is a body pushing, the other is ground that does not yield easily.

But the rune drawn here is Uruz alone, and Uruz does not speak of stillness. It shows the bull's weight and the effort of one hoof lifting free of the bog. Whatever holds you, the reading points at the strength being spent, not at what stands against it.

Isa is ice, and ice holds a thing still. Set against Uruz, the two do not blend — they stand opposed, and you can feel that in the reading already. The bull's force goes almost entirely into lifting one hoof free, and the bog holds what it holds.

Only Uruz was drawn here. What it carries is raw power meeting something that does not give way easily, and the cost of each movement showing plainly in the effort.

Isa is ice, held still. Carried alongside Uruz, it does not soften the force in the reading, nor does it stop it. The bull still lifts its hoof, and the bog still holds.

What the drawn rune holds is the effort itself — the weight of a body working against ground that gives. Isa may mean that effort meets something that does not move easily, or that stillness is simply the shape your strength takes for now. But the reading was Uruz, and Uruz shows the lifting, not the standing.

Isa is ice, the still thing that holds its shape. Set beside Uruz, the two do not blend — one is the bull heaving a hoof from the bog, the other is water gone hard and unmoving.

What was drawn here is Uruz alone. The reading holds force in motion, weight shifting, the strain of lifting free. If stillness belongs anywhere in that, it is only the ground the bull has not yet reached.
